% Both xr and xr-hyper, xr-hyper first, without hyperref. The page
% builds, and each reference prints as with xr alone: from an .aux that
% LaTeX wrote, whose \externaldocument gives the URL of its PDF, its number
% and page, with no link and no URL; from an .aux that tex4ht wrote, with
% its .xref, a link to that document's page.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{xr}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}[https://example.org/ext.pdf]
\externaldocument[T-]{test-xr/tex4ht}
\begin{document}
CaseF \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}.

CaseG \ref{T-oss}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
